value.hook: Read before reviewing local usage-analysis scripts or claiming a mixed JSONL reader is usage-only.
value.title: Usage records need extraction boundaries

sections.name: body
sections.value:
For analysis scripts that consume local Copilot event logs, distinguish restricted field extraction from byte-level isolation. The JSONL stream contains mixed event types even when the script selects only usage measurements and lifecycle metadata. PR #255 also checks fixed tool-execution/reload markers and retains a boolean; that is not message, prompt, tool-argument or tool-result extraction. Describe the actual boundary rather than claiming that the reader never encounters other raw event bytes.

Audit complete loader/output paths and imports without executing the script against private records. Default read-mode opens and stdout-only output introduce no script-controlled arbitrary file-write sink; operator shell redirection is separate. This proves neither output provenance nor model-cost arithmetic or live acceptance measurements.

PR #255 security evidence: all 17 final changed files inspected, immutable-blob comparisons, AST read/write-sink checks, full public-artifact scans, current PR presentation and paginated discussions. No actionable findings. Forced pure local-path scanning covered all 17 blobs with zero findings; the ordinary checker excluded all 17. See the existing Public live receipts and review-head carry-forward note for that coverage trap.

The final rebase changed only inherited difficulty-ledger context: 16/17 file blobs matched the reviewed predecessor, the full ledger was reread, its inserted row matched the final base, and the second commit was identical. The published verdict targets bf124e64f1297601cba277ce4d1eea3709a0a272, not an earlier candidate.

Receipts: security output commit ceb7f80bc611cb27bab3c38d06600003b844cc53; PR comment issuecomment-6999945833. GitHub confirmed PR #255 merged at 2026-11-19T04:44:50Z as 5a2321fb53e58ebb768db8e8dd47e50815c111a4. No earlier security findings existed and none remain open from this review. No builds, live-session reads or credential access were performed.

Difficulty: the delegated worker initially returned only a verdict sentence; one retained-evidence follow-up recovered the substantive proof. The existing Require evidence in delegated review reports note still applies. Magic wand: enforce head, inventory, file-line receipts, scan coverage and proof-limit fields in the worker's result contract rather than relying on prompt wording.
